observation_summary: When calling reset() on a mock object that has been configured with invocation listeners, the listeners are lost, causing subsequent verification of those listeners to fail.
hypothesis: The resetMock method in MockUtil was incorrectly re-initializing the mock handler by creating a new filter with default settings, effectively discarding the existing configuration (including listeners) associated with the original mock handler.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying resetMock to preserve the original mock settings (including listeners) when creating the new filter, rather than resetting to default settings.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows that the original code was creating a new filter with default settings (RETURNS_DEFAULTS), while the fixed code uses the settings from the old mock handler (oldMockHandler.getMockSettings()). This confirms that the original implementation was discarding the existing configuration.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a procedural error in how the mock is reset. The original implementation failed to preserve the existing configuration (specifically the invocation listeners) during the reset process. This is a logic error in the method's implementation of the reset operation, making it an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The diff shows the removal of 'new MockHandler<T>(oldMockHandler)' and the replacement of the filter creation logic.
The failing test 'ListenersLostOnResetMockTest' confirms that listeners are lost after reset.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While it involves initialization of a new filter, the root cause is the procedural logic of how the mock state is reconstructed, which is more accurately described as an algorithmic/methodological error.
The issue is not about the relationship between two separate entities, but rather the internal logic of how one entity (the mock) is correctly reset.
